meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (People's Republic of China) - target jurisdiction for WFOE incorporation; note Taiwan as investor origin
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law with socialist legal characteristics, emerging administrative regulations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) - investment protection provisions
PRC Foreign Investment Law (中华人民共和国外商投资法) effective 2020

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act 公司法 (Articles 128, 129, 154-156, 172, 387) and the Investment Approval regime under the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area (Articles 73 and 93) administered by the MOEA Investment Commission; foreign-invested company formation is additionally governed by the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals 外国投资条例.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs — One-Stop Business Registration Window and Online Company Registration System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (公司设立登记申请书) filed electronically via the MOEA Company Registration Online System (公司登记主题网).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a limited liability company under Taiwanese law; however, the subscribed capital must be fully paid in and evidenced by a bank certificate issued for a segregated capital escrow account held under the proposed company name, which is released only after registration is approved; mainland Chinese investors remain subject to Investment Commission approval ceilings and sector screening.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation application of the Company be approved and the Articles of Incorporation as submitted be adopted; that the initial share subscription by the sole shareholder be accepted and the paid-in capital deposited and certified in the designated escrow bank account; that the registered office be fixed at the address notified to the Central Authority; that the first directors and officers, namely Chairperson, General Manager and Company Secretary, be appointed with immediate effect; that corporate seal, statutory books and bank accounts be opened; that the prompt filing of registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, together with all required industry, food safety and environmental permits, be authorized; and that every officer be empowered to execute all incidental instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment and Mainland Investor Screening Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Investment Commission (投资审议委员会)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Foreign Investment Application (外国人投资申请书) and, for mainland-source capital, the Mainland Investment Approval Application (大陆地区投资许可申请书), with company name, proposed capital amount, shareholder identity, business scope ISIC 5610 restaurant operation, and source-of-funds evidence. The application is reviewed online and the approval letter must be obtained before any capital remittance or bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Passport/ID and residence proof of legal representative and shareholders
Bank reference letter showing source of funds
Business plan and projected financial statements
Power of attorney to the local filing agent
Certificate of incorporation and articles of parent entity (if corporate investor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, submit supplementary evidentiary documents within the statutory 14-day cure period; if sector restriction is triggered, narrow the business scope to permitted items and re-file; if approval is denied on capital-source concern, provide notarized bank statements and a revised source-of-funds explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Registered Office Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA One-Stop Business Registration Window (公司名称及所营事业预查)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name pre-approval application (预先查名) with the proposed Chinese company name, English name (optional), and the business scope item '餐饮业/餐食业 (ISIC 5610-04)'. The authority checks the name against the national company registry for identical or confusingly similar registrations and reserves the name for two months.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, file a new name proposal or submit a statement of consent from the prior registrant; if the reservation lapses, reapply with proof of the pending incorporation submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Escrow Account and Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank qualified to issue capital verification certificates under MOEA regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a segregated escrow account 'Application Deposit Account for Incorporation of [Company Name]' in the proposed company name and remit the full subscribed paid-in capital from the foreign shareholder. Obtain a bank capital verification certificate (存款证明书) confirming the capital amount and the account holder's identity, which serves as evidence of paid-in capital for registration.
required_dossiers: Passport/ID copies of legal representative and shareholders
Bank account opening forms and customer due diligence package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries beneficial ownership, provide an organizational chart and source-of-funds statements; if remittance currency is restricted, obtain central bank foreign exchange approval and re-execute the wire transfer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Registration at MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs — Online Company Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Company Registration (公司设立登记申请书) online, attaching the notarized articles of incorporation, the capital verification certificate, the lease agreement for the registered office, and the identification of duly appointed directors and officers. The filing covers issuance of the company registration certificate (公司登记证明书) and the unified business tax number (统一编号).
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (公司章程)
Registered office lease contract and landlord consent letter
Power of attorney to the filing agent
Identification documents of legal representative and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice (补正通知), complete the correction within the statutory 15-day cure period; if the application is rejected, re-file after rectifying capital verification or officer eligibility issues; re-submission is permitted without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Business Certificate and Labor Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (税务局) and Local Government Business Administration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the MOEA one-stop inter-agency service, activate the unified business tax number, register as a VAT business and public issuance invoice (统一发票) purchaser, apply for abuse tax registration, and register the employer with the labor insurance and national health insurance bureaus before commencing payroll or operations.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease contract and usage permit
Business premises fire safety compliance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office flags unverified street address for the unified business number, provide a supplementary premises usage certificate; if the lease does not meet the tax office's place-of-business requirements, amend the lease or provide a sublease consent letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Registration and Sanitation Permit Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Health, Taipei City Government (or local health bureau) under the Ministry of Health and Welfare
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Food Business Registration (食品业者登记) application with the local health department, which records the establishment under Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation, and schedule the compulsory sanitation inspection of the Malatang kitchen, self-serve ingredient counter and soup broth preparation area. Obtain the Health Management Inspection Report as a precondition of the operating license.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and unified business number
Layout plan of the food premises
Certificates of food safety manager (nutrition/dietetics qualified employee)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the health department orders rectification after inspection, complete remediation within the fixed deadline and re-inspect; if the food safety manager certificate is insufficient, hire a new qualified officer and submit amended registration; cite compliance with Taiwan food safety standards and HACCP guidance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises Permit and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire Bureau and Department of Urban Development, Taipei City Government
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Fire Safety Installation Check (消防安全设备检查) and obtain the Equipment Inspection Certificate, secure the building's legal use certificate (使用执照) confirming restaurant usage, install fire alarm and extinguishing systems, and pass the local fire brigade's on-site inspection before opening to the public.
required_dossiers: Building use certificate and lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection fails, prepare a corrective action plan, install all missing equipment and apply for re-inspection; if the building's use certificate excludes restaurant use, apply for a change-of-use permit with the Department of Urban Development prior to re-filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health and Welfare, Food and Drug Administration (卫生福利部食品药物管理署) through the local Municipal Health Bureau; operational authorization and signage additionally governed by the Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration Certificate (食品业者登记证) and Restaurant Establishment Sanitation Approval (餐饮场所卫生核准证明), together with a business certificate under the Commercial Registration Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (行政院环境保护署) and local Environmental Protection Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — Exempted from full EIA Report; subject to self-managed environmental registration, local wastewater discharge permit and pollutant declaration for the self-serve restaurant operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent compliance with Taiwan Water Pollution Control Act effluent standards (COD ≤ 100 mg/L, BOD ≤ 30 mg/L, SS ≤ 30 mg/L after grease trap treatment); kitchen cooking fume extraction with oil mist filters and odor control maintaining visible emissions at zero opacity and VOC emissions within local air pollution control district limits; waste oil and oil residue must be collected by licensed waste haulers under the Waste Management Act manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Municipal Fire Bureau, including fire alarm, extinguisher and emergency exit compliance; structural load inspection and building use certificate for restaurant occupancy confirming IBC-compliant floor loads for the broth stations and refrigerated counters; occupational workplace clearance through the Labor Inspection Office covering electrical safety, hot liquid handling procedures, slip-resistant flooring, and food-handler hygiene certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (財政部, MOF), operating through the five Regional National Taxation Bureaus (各地區國稅局) and the Taipei and Kaohsiung National Taxation Bureaus. Primary digital portals: MOF Tax Entry Portal (財政部稅務入口網, etax.nat.gov.tw), the E-Invoice Government Integrated Platform (電子發票整合服務平台, einvoice.nat.gov.tw), and the Electronic Tax Filing and Payment Service (財政部電子申報繳稅服務網, tax.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The non-resident shareholder of this WFOE-type LLC obtains investment approval from the MOEA Investment Commission under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (which also governs mainland-China investors transiting through third jurisdictions). Step 2: Filing of company incorporation registration (公司登記) with the MOEA or an authorized local commerce authority. Step 3: Under the 2023 one-stop reform, the incorporation filing concurrently constitutes the statutory tax registration (稅籍登記); the system automatically assigns the eight-digit Unified Business Number (統一編號, GUI), which serves as the corporate income tax account number, the VAT registration number, and the e-invoice issuer identification. Step 4: The company activates its e-invoice credentials, registers a software vendor on the E-Invoice Government Platform, and applies for the first allotment of invoice number series (發票字軌). Step 5: Where goods or services are to be exported, the company separately obtains a Customs Administration registered importer/exporter code. The foreign parent is not required to hold a Taiwan GUI unless it independently earns Taiwan-source income; the WFOE, regardless of foreign ownership, is always classified as a domestic Taiwan 'profit-seeking enterprise'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Tax-Exempt_Zone not applicable. The WFOE is a resident profit-seeking enterprise (營利事業) with head office in Taiwan and is subject to corporate income tax at 20% on Taiwan-source income and, where applicable, foreign-source income integrated with foreign tax credit; an additional retained-earnings tax of 5% applies to unappropriated surplus where profits are not distributed. The entity is not pass-through eligible; dividends remitted to the foreign parent are subject to non-resident dividend withholding at 21% absent an applicable treaty or cross-strait arrangement. No free-trade-zone income exemption is available for the onshore restaurant and franchise operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election or hybrid-entity election exists in Taiwan. Available elections include: (1) the Blue Return election (藍色申報書) with CPA-attested financial statements, preserving the 10-year net operating loss carryforward under Income Tax Act Article 39; (2) the deemed-profits election under Article 25 for qualifying international transport and technical services; (3) Business Innovation Act elections for R&D tax credits, qualified investment expensing, and IP disposal gains; (4) the OECD Pillar Two framework, effective in Taiwan from 2025 for groups exceeding EUR 750 million consolidated revenue, involving a Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax and Income Inclusion Rule that are mandatory rather than elective; (5) anti-hybrid provisions (Income Tax Act Articles 43-3 and 43-4) and CFC rules effective from tax year 2023 which override hybrid instrument outcomes; elections must be filed with the National Taxation Bureau prior to the annual return deadline and, once made, bind subsequent assessment years.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅法) - a credit-invoice value-added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Every legal-entity profit-seeking enterprise, including this WFOE LLC, is mandatorily registered for business tax (稅籍登記) from commencement of business irrespective of turnover. The only statutory de minimis exemption in the Business Tax Act applies to natural-person small-scale operators with average monthly sales below NT$80,000 for goods and NT$40,000 for restaurant services; the threshold is not available to corporate taxpayers. The WFOE's restaurant and franchise operations, with expected monthly sales exceeding NT$200,000 per outlet, are fully liable for 5% VAT and must issue uniform invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE is obliged to issue statutory Uniform Invoices (統一發票) for all B2B and B2C sales. E-invoice issuance is mandatory for newly registered taxpayers; invoices must be transmitted through MOF-certified software to the E-Invoice Government Integrated Platform within 48 hours for B2B transactions and within 7 calendar days for B2C transactions under the current E-Invoice Implementation Directions. The MOF is phasing in same-day real-time clearance (即時上傳): already required for newly registered entities since 2022 and scheduled for all e-invoice issuers by 2026. Transmission uses HTTPS web-service APIs or the TURNKEY gateway with two-factor certificate-based mutual authentication. There is no physical fiscal stamp; compliance is evidenced by the government-allotted invoice number series (發票字軌) embedded in the invoice QR code and the certified platform upload timestamp. Failure to transmit within the statutory window gives rise to per-invoice administrative fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (零稅率) is available under Business Tax Act Article 7 for: (a) goods physically exported from Taiwan, evidenced by a customs export declaration; (b) services sold to foreign enterprises or institutions for use outside Taiwan, including master franchise licensing, brand licensing, central kitchen know-how, training and management fees invoiced to overseas franchisees, provided the services are not used within Taiwan and consideration is received in foreign currency; (c) services directly connected with cross-border international transport. Domestic Malatang self-serve restaurant sales, local POS receipts, and royalties from Taiwan franchisees remain taxable at 5%. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated sales is refundable through the periodic VAT return; the National Taxation Bureau applies a strict evidentiary nexus between the declared export, the foreign-currency inward remittance, and the underlying contract.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) showing the WFOE's registered exporter code, for all goods movements
Signed master franchise or licensing agreement and a service delivery or performance certificate, for zero-rated service exports
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or logistics release documentation evidencing physical shipment
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (外匯收入結匯水單/匯入匯款證明書) issued by a permitted Taiwan bank, clearly matched to the corresponding invoice

Foreign-currency commercial invoice, and, where required by the taxing authority, a certificate of offshore consumption or destination-market regulatory approval (e.g., food hygiene registration for exported Malatang broth base and condiments)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau cross-matches zero-rating claims against customs export data, e-invoice records, bank foreign-exchange settlement files, and licensing agreements. A refund obtained without genuine physical export, offshore service performance, or foreign-currency repatriation is retroactively reversed with interest computed at the Postal Savings one-year fixed deposit rate. Administrative penalties include a fine of one to five times the underpaid tax under Business Tax Act Article 51, possible suspension of business, and, where false documents or a fraudulent scheme are established, criminal liability under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act with imprisonment of up to five years and monetary fines. Reassessment and clawback remain open for up to seven tax years in cases involving fraud or intentional concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating as the PBOC-affiliated foreign-exchange regulator.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains RMB convertibility for current-account transactions under IMF Article VIII; capital-account transactions remain subject to SAFE registration, verifiable documentation, and macro-prudential controls. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) may freely settle genuine current-account receipts (sales, royalties, service fees) into RMB through a licensed domestic bank. Profit distribution to the Taiwan shareholder is treated as a controlled current-account remittance: it is permissible only after (i) the annual financial statements are audited, (ii) the corporate income tax and any dividend withholding tax are settled, (iii) a shareholder resolution declares the dividend, and (iv) the bank completes SAFE authenticity review. No prior SAFE approval is required for each profit remittance, but the transaction must be recorded under SAFE's cross-border payment reporting system. The principal obstacles are: unfiled annual FDI information reports, undocumented related-party transactions, outstanding tax/Fines, breach of the capital account negative list, and failure to establish distributable profits. Equity capital injected into the WFOE is irrevocably classified as capital-account funds; principal cannot be repatriated to the Taiwan shareholder except through a liquidating resolution, capital reduction registration, or approved share transfer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China does not impose fixed mandatory surrender ratios for export proceeds. Exporters may retain 100% of qualifying trade receipts in a domestic current-account foreign-exchange account or convert them to RMB at the onshore market rate through a licensed bank. Under SAFE's Trade in Goods monitoring regime, export proceeds must be repatriated through an authorized banking channel within the contractual payment term; where collection occurs more than 90 days after the export customs declaration date, the WFOE must complete deferred-collection registration in SAFE's monitoring platform before settlement. Non-repatriation of export proceeds without an underlying cross-border credit/loan structure is not permissible and triggers SAFE post-event verification, possible penalties, and downgrading of the enterprise's compliance classification. The WFOE in the malatang self-serve franchise business should be classified as a 'B' enterprise under SAFE's trade-in-goods categorization, meaning standard documentary review applies to every foreign-exchange receipt and payment.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs), such as Airwallex, DBS, or Revolut Business, cannot lawfully serve as the primary onshore account provider for the Chinese WFOE. They are not licensed by PBOC/SAFE to conduct domestic RMB clearing, local POS settlement, VAT-linked receipt collection, or SAFE-reportable cross-border payments for a mainland-incorporated company. Their use is limited to supplementary offshore multi-currency treasury vehicles for the Taiwan parent entity, and even that ancillary use requires compliance with Taiwan's foreign-exchange and corporate banking regulations. All onshore operating cash flows, royalty-related remittances, and foreign-exchange transactions must pass through a PRC-licensed commercial bank; routing them through an offshore EMI without a domestic banking relationship would violate SAFE's requirement that cross-border receipts and payments be settled by authorized institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and PBOC customer due diligence rules, a WFOE opening an RMB basic deposit account or an FDI capital account must complete face-to-face KYC verification. In practice, the WFOE's legal representative or the authorized signatory must appear physically at the mainland bank branch for an interview; remote video account opening is available only in narrow pilot programs and is generally not granted to foreign-invested enterprises with capital-account exposures. If the legal representative is a Taiwan resident, original Taiwan passport and Mainland Travel Permit must be presented, and the Taiwan shareholder's board resolutions, identity documents, and financial statements must pass cross-strait notarization and authentication. A notarized power of attorney may permit the onshore general manager to attend the interview, but the bank will typically require a supplementary video confirmation with the Taiwan UBO. SAFE account registration procedures for the capital account cannot be delegated solely to an offshore service provider without an onshore licensed account-opening bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait ownership chain with no clear commercial substance, especially if the Taiwan shareholder is a Hong Kong or BVI intermediate holding company rather than the actual Taiwan operating party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full legal ownership diagram; explain each layer's tax and governance purpose; submit the Taiwan parent's company registration, audited financial statements, the franchise master license agreement, the mainland WFOE's lease, food-service operating license, and a projected funding-and-cash-flow model demonstrating the physical restaurant operations and the royalty channel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the PBOC ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration and the SAFE FDI registration record, often caused by outdated Taiwan shareholder resolutions or stale cross-strait notarization.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a reconciled UBO register showing every natural person holding 25% or more of the Taiwan parent; match it against the SAFE Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration form; attach fresh Taiwan court/notary authenticated resolutions and the corroborating cross-strait document verification letter; where a manager has unintended control, add a signed statement explaining indirect control mechanisms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection routed from a third-party entity or from a Taiwan financial institution without proof that the remitting entity is the true investor, creating a source-of-funds suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the Taiwan shareholder's bank reference letter, audited financials or liquidation certificates, a capital source and wealth explanation (salary, dividends, asset sale), the signed capital contribution statement, and the SWIFT confirmation that ties the inbound wire to the SAFE FDI registration; avoid any third-party remitter; if third-party payment is unavoidable, file a formal cross-border payment agreement and authenticate it under cross-strait rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive restaurant business with high-frequency local POS deposits that appear inconsistent with declared revenue, inventory purchases, and tax returns; a red flag under AML surveillance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Install a bank-certified POS and payment aggregator system with daily settlement statements; reconcile POS transaction records to the WFOE's enterprise resource planning system; maintain supplier invoices, kitchen inventory logs, employee attendance/社保 records, and quarterly VAT and corporate income tax filings; provide a written cash-management policy stating that all cash receipts are banked intact on T+1.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent should wire the registered FDI equity capital via SWIFT MT103 directly to the WFOE's dedicated SAFE-registered 'FDI foreign-exchange capital account' at the designated tier-1 Chinese bank. Prior to remittance, the WFOE must obtain the SAFE Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration certificate (业务登记凭证) and open the capital account under the bank's direct registration mechanism. The wire instruction must clearly designate the transaction type as 'Foreign Direct Investment - Capital Contribution' and use the correct SAFE/BOP transaction nature code for FDI inbound capital formation. The bank will perform authenticity review, anti-money-laundering screening, and capital account income control checks. Upon receipt, the foreign-exchange funds may be settled into RMB through the bank, with proceeds credited to the WFOE's 'RMB capital settlement account' (结汇待支付账户), subject to the negative list. For RMB-denominated inbound investment, the Taiwan parent may channel the funds through Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) using RMB SWIFT-equivalent messaging; in all cases, the bank must record the transaction against the FDI registration and issue the corresponding cross-border receipts declaration. No unregistered inbound remittance may be accepted into an operational account for use as equity capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for ingredient imports, self-service equipment, and the franchise royalty should run through the following clearing rails: (i) routine royalty and service-fee remittances to the Taiwan parent via SWIFT MT103 under the bank's service trade payment verification, supported by the royalty agreement, tax withholding certificates, and an invoice; (ii) large-scale cross-border procurement of kitchen equipment and bulk packaged ingredients via an at-sight commercial Letter of Credit issued by the mainland bank, with presentation through the Taiwan beneficiary's negotiating bank; (iii) domestic RMB supplier disbursements through CNAPS real-time gross settlement from the WFOE's RMB operational account; and (iv) cross-border RMB payments, where the Taiwan supplier accepts RMB, processed through CIPS with full tax documentation. Every outbound royalty wire must be entered under the international receipts/payments reporting system with the nature code for trademark/franchise license fees; amounts must be consistent with the prior year's sales-based royalty calculation and transfer-pricing documentation. The bank will require evidence that no PRC tax liabilities are outstanding and that VAT withholding and stamp tax, where applicable, have been paid.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD foreign-exchange forwards for the WFOE's genuine current-account and capital-account exposures, with maturity and size consistent with the underlying franchise royalty and procurement flows.

Onshore FX swaps (foreign-exchange swap contracts) used for temporary liquidity conversion between RMB and foreign currency, subject to SAFE's real-transaction-background requirement and bank credit limits.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for medium- and long-term hedging of the WFOE's foreign-currency liability or equity exposure, provided the swap is approved by the domestic bank and has a clearly documented underlying exposure.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted onshore for the PRC WFOE; the Taiwan parent may employ offshore NDF contracts to hedge Taiwan-dollar/USD exposure, but such instruments cannot be booked by the mainland entity and will not be recognized by SAFE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Taiwan corporate income tax annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the relevant jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May following the taxable year; filing is generally due by 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine generally applies for late filing; additional tax, interest, estimated assessment, and penalties may apply. Repeated non-compliance may trigger enforcement and tax registration consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement audit or certification, where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau and, where applicable, Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent company-registration authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Complete before the corporate income tax filing deadline and retain supporting records for the statutory retention period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain required audit or certification may cause rejection or adjustment of the tax filing, administrative penalties, tax reassessment, and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company basic-information and beneficial-owner information confirmation or update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or designated company-registration authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirm or update upon the prescribed annual or authority-request cycle and promptly after any reportable change in directors, shareholders, controlling persons, or beneficial owners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines may apply for failure to report, inaccurate reporting, or failure to correct information. Continued non-compliance may result in compulsory inspection, restriction of registration services, or other enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No routine filing authority; corporate records must be maintained for inspection and statutory compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinarily within six months after the end of each financial year, unless a lawful extension or alternative schedule applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or document the meeting may result in director liability, shareholder remedies, inability to evidence approvals, and administrative penalties where a statutory filing or approval is affected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food-business permit and sanitary-license renewal or annual operational compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Relevant local government health, food-safety, or business-registration authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: According to the validity period and renewal cycle of the food-business registration, permit, or local operating approval; no uniform national annual renewal date applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines, corrective orders, suspension, compulsory closure, permit cancellation, and potential criminal liability may apply for operating without a valid approval or violating food-safety requirements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified public accountant audit or certification may be required for public companies, companies subject to sector-specific rules, and private companies meeting statutory capital, revenue, employee, or other prescribed thresholds. The exact obligation must be confirmed against the entity's paid-in capital, revenue, employment level, ownership, and industry status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards, substantially converged with IFRS, subject to Taiwan-specific statutory accounting and tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain current records of members, directors, controlling persons, and ultimate beneficial owners. Report prescribed changes to the competent authority within the applicable statutory period and complete any required annual or authority-requested confirmation. Share transfers must be supported by transfer instruments, updated ownership records, and required registration or tax documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-2,500 per year, excluding mail forwarding, nominee services, licensing support, and extraordinary filings.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-12,000 per year for a small private company; higher for audited entities with regulated food operations, foreign ownership, multiple outlets, or significant transaction volume.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for a WFOE in Taiwan. The 20% rate applies to net taxable income; an additional 5% retained earnings surtax is imposed when undistributed earnings accumulate beyond prescribed limits. Targeted incentives exist for R&D and certain strategic industries under the Statute for Industrial Innovation (e.g., up to 15% R&D credit and accelerated depreciation for automated machinery), but typical franchise and food-service operations do not qualify for blanket exemptions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書); e-filed via the Ministry of Finance electronic filing and payment portal (tax.nat.gov.tw) using the approved 'Profit-Seeking Enterprise Filing System' with digital certificate or delegated accountant credentials.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year fiscal year, the filing window is 1 May through 31 May of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year approved by the tax authority, the return must be filed within five months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal company name, Unified Business Number (8-digit GUI), ISIC classification code (5610 mapping), head office address, and fiscal year-end. Attach the certificate of incorporation and, for WFOE, the investment approval or foreign-investment registration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Taiwan branch or subsidiary identification only. Non-resident shareholders' details are disclosed on separate ownership schedules; identity of ultimate beneficial owner is required under AML due diligence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 02: Income Recognition and Base Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare gross revenue from franchise royalty income, initial franchise fees, commissary sales, and other operating turnover. The accrual basis is mandatory for companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE receives franchise fees from overseas related parties, those amounts must be included in taxable turnover and separately categorized for transfer pricing disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 03: Cost of Goods Sold / Operating Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report cost of sales, franchise support costs, inventory of malatang broth ingredients and dry goods, and direct labor costs. Include auditable ledgers and requisition documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border purchases from related PRC suppliers must be supported by transfer pricing analysis and commercial invoices; importing costs must reconcile with customs filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List payroll, rent, marketing, depreciation, administrative overhead, and franchise training expenses. Expense deduction requires statutory invoices and wage withholding records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties for management fees or procurement services are deductible only if they satisfy the arm's-length standard and are not royalties disguised as service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 07: Reconciliation from Book Income to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add or subtract permanent and temporary differences, including tax-exempt income, non-deductible penalties, exchange-rate gains/losses, and deferred tax items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any deemed income from transactions adjusted under Article 43-1 is entered as temporary differences to the extent tax authorities make an upward transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10: Tax Credits and Prepaid Taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset taxes withheld at source, quarterly estimated payments, investment tax credits, and foreign tax credits. Attach supporting schedules for every credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE, withholding taxes borne on overseas royalty income might generate a foreign tax credit if the income has been subject to foreign income tax and is taxable in Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 11: Income Tax Payable and Retained Earnings Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory 20% rate on taxable income, compute the regular income tax, and then calculate the 5% retained earnings surtax on undistributed earnings above the accumulation threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The return must include retained earnings surtax even where all shareholders have agreed to retain earnings for reinvestment; separate form schedules are required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 14: Auditor's Certificate and Related Party Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For entities exceeding the statutory threshold, attach a CPA-reviewed or audited financial report and the related-party transaction summary schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent company holding 25% or more of the WFOE is a related party; all transactions with it must be fully disclosed in the related-party schedule regardless of amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with no extension: an additional 3% of the tax payable per month or part of a month, capped at 30%; if the return is not filed by the end of two months after the statutory deadline, the tax authority may assess tax on the basis of available information and impose a fine of up to 2–3 times the underpaid tax. Interest accrues daily on late tax payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Payment (暫繳) form; e-filed or paid at any designated financial institution or via the same MOF tax payment portal using unified number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual estimated payment (generally due once per year for the July–December period)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment fall between 1 September and 30 September of the current assessment year, based on one-half of the immediately preceding year's taxable income, unless an exemption under Article 67(3) applies when zero or minimal taxable income is expected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line A: Estimated Taxable Income Basis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the most recent year's taxable income divided by two, or an approved forecast for the current year if filing under projected income method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE in Taiwan must use the statutory presumptive method unless it obtains an ex ante tax authority approval for net-profit forecasting; foreign-owned entities are not exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Multiply estimated taxable income by 20% and subtract any tax-deductible investment credits, withholding from domestic sources, and prior overpayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim credit on this form; the WFOE must remit the full provisional tax with its own funds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm the WFOE's responsible person and accountant details, and certify accuracy under penalty of perjury.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The responsible director resident in Taiwan must sign; directors residing abroad may appoint a local agent with a power of attorney.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late provisional payment: a surcharge of 1.2% of the undue provisional tax for every 15-day delay, capped at 12%; a returned check increases the surcharge to 24% of the unpaid amount. The full outstanding amount remains immediately collectible.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on gross dividends distributed by a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise to a non-resident shareholder without a fixed place of business in Taiwan. Resident shareholders are not subject to withholding on distributions, but undistributed earnings are taxed at the 5% retained earnings surtax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce the 21% withholding under a comprehensive income tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of its jurisdiction; (ii) submit the TRC and a completed 'Application for Reduced Withholding Tax under Tax Treaty' to the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau before the payment date; and (iii) evidence beneficial ownership and substantive commercial presence. Approval generally takes 2–4 weeks and is renewable for subsequent calendar years. As of this filing, no effective DTA exists between mainland China and Taiwan, so a PRC shareholder of the WFOE cannot invoke treaty relief; the 21% rate will apply to any approved dividend distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalty payments for franchise IP (trademarks, know-how, trade names) is 20%; statutory withholding on cross-border interest is also 20% (15% where paid by financial institutions to foreign lenders). Under Taiwan's enacted DTAs, common treaty-reduced rates are 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and TRC evidence; given the PRC–Taiwan scenario, the full 20% statutory rates apply to a mainland-related franchise or financing contract.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The WFOE must prepare a transfer pricing Local File and supporting comparability analysis when its total Taiwan related-party transaction amount exceeds NT$200 million in a fiscal year, or when the expected annual transaction value with a related party in a low-tax jurisdiction exceeds NT$50 million. A Group Master File is due when the MNE group's consolidated revenue exceeds NT$5 billion; Cross-Border Country-by-Country filing is mandatory when the ultimate parent entity's group revenue exceeds NT$27 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not apply EU-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) verbatim, but the 'substance-over-form' doctrine is enforced through Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act and the anti-tax-haven purpose provisions. A WFOE engaged solely in collecting franchise royalties without local staffing, operational management, or real franchising activity may be disregarded; the tax authority can attribute the income to the actual economic owner and impose penalties. The WFOE must maintain a Taiwan operating office, local employees, board decisions book, bank accounts, and ongoing franchise support records to establish genuine business substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting franchise royalty income, POS terminal sales, and commission fees from self-serve malatang stores; destroying or refusing to present cash register data; using unreported private we-chat or cash receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imposition of underpaid tax plus a fine of 2–3 times the concealed amount; daily interest accrual; referral to criminal investigation under the Tax Collection Act, with imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine of up to NT$30 million in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false tax returns are personally liable for the monetary penalty to the extent of the evaded tax; the court may order travel bans and seizure of personal assets; culpable officers face imprisonment and loss of civil rights.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal WFOE with no physical kitchen, management personnel, franchise support, or decision-making in Taiwan; depositing franchise fees into offshore accounts and sending all profits to the mainland parent; filing nil tax returns while granting licences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may recharacterize the entire transaction, disallow intercompany deductions, and assess tax directly on the beneficial owner; the company may be deregistered; non-compliance with corporate filing obligations triggers an administrative fine from NT$10,000 to NT$500,000, plus an additional 3x penalty on hidden profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the veil where there is an abuse of legal personality; directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and civil restitution; failure to maintain a valid registered office can lead to automatic dissolution and a separate per-director criminal penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Red Flags and Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funnelling daily over-the-counter cash through unregistered aggregators, structuring transfers to avoid the NT$500,000 AML reporting threshold, or using shell trading companies to mask the identity of franchise fee recipients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, conviction carries imprisonment of 3–7 years and a fine of up to NT$50 million if aggravated; repeat corporate offenders may be barred from holding franchise licences; assets are forfeited.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face immediate individual criminal liability; each director can be fined up to NT$10 million and banned from leaving Taiwan; the court may impose a 10-year prohibition on serving as a director of any domestic company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting franchise royalty rates to the mainland related party below arm's length, overpaying for raw material imports, or accumulating controlled losses in Taiwan without legitimate commercial reasons; failure to prepare and present the mandatory Local File or Master File within audit deadlines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Taxation Bureau adjusts taxable income upward to reflect an arm's-length consideration; the adjusted tax may be subject to a 100% penalty under Article 110; interest and daily surcharge accrue; in a serious case involving a tax haven entity, a 200% penalty and criminal referral may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Chief Executives and Chief Financial Officers who certify false transfer pricing documentation are jointly liable for the underpaid tax if the company fails to collect; repeated willful adjustments result in disqualification from serving as responsible persons and potential travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or branch profits to a foreign or mainland-China shareholder without executing 21% or 20% withholding; filing the withholding return late; or classifying dividend distributions as loans to evade WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority collects the missed withholding amount from the WFOE directly, adds a fine equal to 1.5–3 times the withheld amount for deliberate non-compliance, and levies late payment interest; serious cases trigger prosecution of the responsible representative.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director is treated as the withholding agent and is personally liable to remit the unpaid withholding; civil tort actions by the government are enforceable against the director's personal estate; travel bans and denial of exit visas are routinely applied.
